title: Chronology
summary: Governs headings for chronology as a science (Chronology; Chronology, [adjective] or [Adjective] chronology; uninverted forms for Indian systems) and the free-floating subdivisions --History--Chronology and --Chronology. Places, corporate bodies, ethnic groups, and topics divisible by --History take --History--Chronology; period-subdivided place history, topics not divided by --History (music, art, literature, inherently historical topics), persons, and sacred works take --Chronology directly. Chronology, Historical is used for world history.
validation_rules: General works on the science of chronology: `Chronology`. (H 1367 sec. 1.a)

Chronology systems of a place, civilization, religion, etc. take `Chronology, [adjectival qualifier]` or `[Adjectival qualifier] chronology`, e.g. `Chronology, Byzantine`, `Jewish chronology`, `Chronology, Mexican`. (H 1367 sec. 1.b)
Exception: chronology systems of Indians use uninverted phrase headings, e.g. `Aztec chronology`, `Maya chronology`, `Indian chronology--Mexico`. (H 1367 sec. 1.b, 3)
Lists of dates and events of world history: `Chronology, Historical`, optionally subdivided by `--Charts, diagrams, etc.` or `--Tables`; not `World history--Chronology`. (H 1367 sec. 2.a, 2.c)
Under names of regions, countries, cities, etc., use `--History--Chronology`, e.g. `United States--History--Chronology`; `[place]--Chronology` directly is not the prescribed form. (H 1367 sec. 2.b)
For a period in the history of a place, use `[place]--History--[period subdivision]--Chronology`, e.g. `Great Britain--History--Victoria, 1837-1901--Chronology`. (H 1367 sec. 2.b)

Under topics that can be subdivided by `--History` (H 1647), use `--History--Chronology`, placed after any geographic subdivision, e.g. `Earthquakes--Mexico--History--Chronology`, `Medicine, Military--United States--History--Chronology`. (H 1367 sec. 2.c, 3)

Under headings not subdivided by `--History` (music, art, literature, inherently historical topics), use `--Chronology` without `--History`, e.g. `Popular music--United States--Chronology`, `Arts, American--Chronology`, `English drama--17th century--Chronology`, `Japan--Economic conditions--1945---Chronology`, `Rock music--Chronology`, `Crusades--First, 1096-1099--Chronology`, `World politics--1945---Chronology`. (H 1367 sec. 2.c, 3)
Do not use `--Chronology` under a topic if a phrase heading for the concept has been established (e.g. use `Chronology, Historical`, not `World history--Chronology`). (H 1367 sec. 2.c)
Under names of individual persons, use `--Chronology` (not `--History--Chronology`), e.g. `Constant, Benjamin, 1767-1830--Chronology`. (H 1367 sec. 2.d, 3)
Under names of individual corporate bodies, use `--History--Chronology`, e.g. `United States. Army Medical Department--History--Chronology`. (H 1367 sec. 2.e, 3)
Under individual ethnic groups, including Indians, use `--History--Chronology`, e.g. `African Americans--History--Chronology`. (H 1367 sec. 2.f, 3)
Under uniform titles of sacred works, use `--Chronology`, e.g. `Book of Mormon--Chronology`, `Bible. Old Testament--Chronology` (coded `$x` for discussions of dating). (H 1367 sec. 2.g, 3)

sections.heading: a. General
sections.text: Assign the heading *Chronology* to general works on the science of arranging time in fixed periods and of dating events and epochs.

sections.heading: b. Special
sections.text:
Assign headings of the type *Chronology, [adjectival qualifier]* or *[Adjectival qualifier] chronology* to works on the system of chronology practiced in a particular place, civilization, religion, etc. Examples:

```
650 #0 $a Chronology, Byzantine.
650 #0 $a Jewish chronology.
650 #0 $a Chronology, Mexican.
```

Exception: To works on the system of arranging time used by Indians, assign phrase headings in uninverted order, for example, *Aztec chronology*.

sections.heading: a. General
sections.text:
Assign the heading *Chronology, Historical* to works containing lists of dates and events of world history in order of occurrence.

Subdivide the heading by the free-floating form subdivision *--Charts, diagrams, etc.*, or by *--Tables*, if appropriate for the work.

sections.heading: b. Places
sections.text:
Use the free-floating subdivision *--History--Chronology* under names of regions, countries, cities, etc., for works that contain listings of dates and events in the history of that place, for example, *United States--History--Chronology*.

Use the free-floating subdivision *--Chronology* under headings of the type *[place]--History--[period subdivision]* for chronologies limited to a particular period in the history of a place, for example, *Great Britain--History--Victoria, 1837-1901--Chronology*.

sections.heading: c. Topics
sections.text:
Use the free-floating subdivision *--Chronology* or *--History--Chronology* under topical headings to works containing listings of dates in order of occurrence pertaining to the topic.

If the topic can be divided by *--History* (see H 1647), use *--History--Chronology*, for example, *Earthquakes--Mexico--History--Chronology*. If the heading is one that is not divided by *--History*, such as headings for music, art, literature, and inherently historical topics, use *--Chronology* without interposing *--History*, for example, *Popular music--United States--Chronology*; *Arts, American--Chronology*; *English drama--17th century--Chronology*; *Japan--Economic conditions--1945- --Chronology*.

Do not use the free-floating subdivision *--Chronology* under a topic if a phrase heading for the concept has been established. Example:

```
650 #0 $a Chronology, Historical.
 [not 650 #0 $a World history $v Chronology.]
```

sections.heading: d. Persons
sections.text: Use the free-floating subdivision *--Chronology* under names of individual persons to works that list by date events in the life of the person, or the dates when a person's works were written or published, as well as discussions of the chronology of such events or works.

sections.heading: e. Corporate bodies
sections.text: Use the free-floating subdivision *--History--Chronology* under names of individual corporate bodies for works listing events and dates in the history of the organization.

sections.heading: f. Ethnic groups
sections.text: Use the free-floating subdivision *--History--Chronology* under individual ethnic groups, including Indians, for works listing events and dates in the history of the group.

sections.heading: g. Sacred works
sections.text: Use the free-floating subdivision *--Chronology* under uniform titles for sacred works for discussions of the dating and order of occurrence of events mentioned in the sacred work, for example, *Book of Mormon--Chronology*.

sections.heading: 3. Examples
sections.text:
```
Title: Essays on Jewish chronology.
650 #0 $a Jewish chronology.
630 00 $a Bible. $p Old Testament $x Chronology.

Title: Chronology of the first crusade.
650 #0 $a Crusades $y First, 1096-1099 $v Chronology.

Title: Two hundred years of military medicine.
610 10 $a United States.  $b Army Medical Department
          $x History $v Chronology.
650 #0 $a Medicine, Military $z United States $x History
          $v Chronology.

Title: Milestone political events : 1945-1975.
650 #0 $a World politics $y 1945- $v Chronology.

Title: A guide to the published works of Benjamin Constant.
600 10 $a Constant, Benjamin, $d 1767-1830 $v Bibliography.
600 10 $a Constant, Benjamin, $d 1767-1830 $v Chronology.

Title: The pages of rock history.
650 #0 $a Rock music $v Chronology.

Title: A chronology of Afro-American history.
650 #0 $a African Americans $x History $v Chronology.

Title: A key to the Mesoamerican reckoning of time.
650 #0 $a Indian chronology $z Mexico.
650 #0 $a Indian chronology $z Central America.
650 #0 $a Maya chronology.
650 #0 $a Aztec chronology.
```
